summary: The ACCV 2026 supplement (/home/spencer/Projects/OnlineSyntheticCorrespondence/ACCV_2026/supp_main.tex, titled "Supplementary Material: Off-Target Mass or Missing Support?") provides six things. (1) Sec. supp:law gives the full per-variant evidence for the regime-direction principle: tab_supp_asym repeats main-paper Table 1 (identical numbers to tables/tab_law.tex) and adds FID/SW2/MMD symmetric baselines, claiming the rule's margin is largest where the directions disagree most (pretrained GLU-Net: rule +0.67/+0.76 vs sym +0.26/+0.33); tab_supp_eps replicates the rule with an epsilon-radius coverage estimator at 1/4/16 px, claiming the rule-over-symmetric margin at 4-16 px exceeds the mean-NN margin while 1 px "saturates"; tab_supp_dino is the appearance-space negative control (all directed correlations -0.15 to -0.35, flip statistic +0.018, p=0.43). (2) Sec. supp:robust (tab_supp_controls, baseline rule rho = +0.507) reports a shuffle null of -0.000 (200 perms, claimed p<0.005), generator-family drops (+0.425 to +0.544), benchmark drops ([+0.495, +0.532]), and size controls (n samples +0.043, n vectors +0.267). (3) Sec. supp:predict gives per-variant reproducibility oracles (pretrained GLU-Net fractions of oracle O2 reach +1.37/+1.31, claimed "fractions >1.3" though the O3 fractions are +1.26/+1.14); gap-stratified pairwise accuracy (rule 0.624/0.652/0.629 overall vs retraining agreement 0.736/0.696 — rule below retraining in every bin, near chance at 0.551-0.569 for sub-1-PCK gaps); a feature-set ablation (mean-NN best for scratch ranking, coverage edges pretrained, appearance max +0.13 though the text says "rho <= 0.16"; the claim that the combined set "gives the best absolute error" is contradicted by epsilon-4px pretrained MAE 7.9 < combined 8.0); a no-table claim that directional anchor interpolation loses to symmetric IDW (16.9 vs 18.9-24.1 held-out-benchmark MAE; 8.6 vs 8.7-10.1 held-out-source); an exclusion note for the pretrained arm of the intervention grid (3 sources whose d_TB and d_BT "orderings coincide", agreeing with transfer on "2 of 3 benchmarks") that CONTRADICTS the main paper's account of the same arm (main.tex ~line 849 reports distinct unstable estimates d_TB +0.64, d_BT +0.31, sym +0.43 "nominally favor[ing] the unmatched direction" — impossible if the orderings coincide); and the full BFV recovery table (KITTI-2015: dolly 2.18, vert. frac 0.001, "camera-centric"; FlyingThings: dolly 0.32, vert. frac 0.920, "object-centric") together with an explicit admission that BFV is blind to the camera/object factorization it is being used to recover. (4) Sec. supp:sampling justifies mean-NN/coverage estimators (rho >= 0.96 at 5e4 vectors, 1.000 at reference; kNN-KL plateaus at 0.5/0.2 and never stabilizes) over "all 110 train->benchmark pairs" — a count that implies 10 benchmarks (11 sources x 10), i.e. includes Middlebury, while the paper's stance is 9 benchmarks; it also concedes the intervention-grid d_TB ranking is "estimator-noise-limited even after 5-seed averaging", which directly qualifies the main paper's pre-registered out-of-sample test. (5) Sec. supp:mid documents the Middlebury exclusion (pretrained eval stuck at 52.6 +/- 4.7 PCK regardless of source; 9 benchmarks, 1,458 models retained) with a sensitivity analysis (flip +0.82 with Middlebury vs +0.90 without; rule rho 0.49/0.50/0.52 vs 0.50/0.51/0.51 — note the no-Middlebury reference triple matches NEITHER the main paper's policy row +0.52/+0.52/+0.50 nor its matched-direction row +0.48/+0.50/+0.49 in tab_predictors.tex). (6) Four figures decompose the absolute predictor into ranking (median per-benchmark slope 0.43-0.51) and level (per-trainset slope 0.93-0.96) and show the closed-loop intervention. Overall the supplement is broadly consistent with the main story but contains one genuine cross-document contradiction (the pretrained grid arm), several text-vs-own-table overstatements (oracle fractions, combined-MAE, "no flip exists" vs RAFT's DINO flip CI [+0.02,+0.16], missing supervision-density row), and several honest admissions that soften the main story (rule below retraining agreement in all gap bins, partial epsilon-replication exactly where the law is strongest, BFV camera/object blind spot, noise-limited d_TB on the intervention family).

claims.claim: Supplement scope: full estimator-replication and appearance-control tables, robustness controls, predictor ablations, sampling stability, the Middlebury exclusion, and additional figures.

Per-variant rule vs directions vs symmetric baselines (mean-NN). Scratch rows: rule equals rho[d_TB], pretrained rows: rule equals rho[d_BT]. Key rows: 'CATs++ -- -- & scratch & +0.53 & +0.53 & +0.03 & +0.46 & +0.38 & +0.39 & +0.30'; 'GLU-Net -- -- & scratch & +0.31 & +0.31 & +0.41 & +0.46'; 'GLU-Net \cmark \cmark & pretrained & +0.76 & -0.22 & +0.76 & +0.33 & +0.33 & +0.28 & +0.05'. Values are identical to main-paper tables/tab_law.tex.

claims.claim: Text claim: 'The rule's margin is largest exactly where the two directions disagree most (pretrained GLU-Net), and the symmetric metrics hedge everywhere.' Supported for pretrained GLU-Net (rule +0.67/+0.76 vs sym +0.26/+0.33) but the same table shows symmetric beating the rule in 4 of 9 rows (e.g., GLU-Net -- cmark scratch: sym +0.58 vs rule +0.37; CATs++ cmark cmark pretrained: sym +0.56, FID +0.62 vs rule +0.50).

Epsilon-radius coverage replication: 'At 4--16 px the rule-over-symmetric margin exceeds the mean-NN margin; 1 px saturates (too strict).' Verified arithmetically from the table on average (mean margin ~+0.13 at 4px, ~+0.11 at 16px vs ~+0.05 for mean-NN; negative at 1px), but replication is uneven: GLU-Net cmark -- pretrained rule is +0.22/+0.27/+0.49 at 1/4/16px vs +0.67 mean-NN.
claims.numbers: GLU-Net cmark cmark pretrained rule: +0.23 / +0.65 / +0.71 vs symmetric +0.19 / +0.47 / +0.50; GLU-Net cmark -- pretrained rule: +0.22 / +0.27 / +0.49

claims.claim: DINO appearance negative control: 'Correlations are weak-to-negative in both directions for every variant; the flip statistic is +0.018 (exact permutation p=0.43) and its leave-one-benchmark-out range crosses zero.' Table directed correlations range -0.15 to -0.35; per-variant flip deltas with 95% CIs.

Robustness controls, baseline fit-free rule rho = +0.507: shuffle null -0.000 (200 perms; text claims empirical p<0.005); drop family kubric +0.544, realflow +0.532, sdf3d +0.515, semantic +0.425, warp2d +0.472; size controls n samples +0.043, n vectors +0.267; drop any single benchmark range [+0.495, +0.532]. Text: family/benchmark drops move the rule 'by at most 0.09'; size-style fit-free rankings reach 'at most rho=0.27'.

Reproducibility oracles per variant: 'Both pretrained GLU-Net variants exceed their oracles (fractions >1.3)'. Table rows: GLU-Net cmark -- pretrained: rule +0.67, O2 +0.49, O3 +0.53, frac O2 +1.37, frac O3 +1.26; GLU-Net cmark cmark pretrained: rule +0.76, O2 +0.58, O3 +0.67, frac O2 +1.31, frac O3 +1.14. Scratch fractions are 0.41-0.77.

Gap-stratified pairwise ordering accuracy (rule, by protocol: src held / bench held / both) vs retraining agreement (same arch / cross arch): bin 0-1: 0.569 / 0.568 / 0.551 vs 0.582 / 0.572; bin >10: 0.675 / 0.725 / 0.689 vs 0.844 / 0.777; ALL: 0.624 / 0.652 / 0.629 vs 0.736 / 0.696. The rule is below retraining agreement in every bin and protocol.

Feature-set ablation for the per-regime linear model (ranking rho src/bench/both held, then MAE): motion mean-NN scratch +0.47/+0.56/+0.48, MAE 10.4; mean-NN pretrained +0.29/+0.50/+0.35, MAE 8.2; epsilon 4px pretrained +0.40/+0.45/+0.39, MAE 7.9; epsilon 1/4/16px scratch +0.26/+0.27/+0.21, MAE 9.4; combined (8) scratch +0.47/+0.39/+0.34, MAE 9.4; combined pretrained +0.43/+0.51/+0.42, MAE 8.0; appearance (DINO) scratch +0.02/+0.13/-0.07, MAE 11.1; appearance pretrained +0.12/+0.10/+0.06, MAE 8.8. Text claims appearance 'rho <= 0.16' and 'the combined set gives the best absolute error'.

Anchor directionality (no table): directional anchor borrowing 'loses to plain symmetric inverse-distance weighting on both anchor-interpolation problems (held-out-benchmark MAE 16.9 symmetric vs 18.9--24.1 directional; held-out-source 8.6 vs 8.7--10.1)'.

Pretrained arm of the intervention grid: 'contains only three sources, whose d_TB and d_BT orderings coincide; it therefore cannot discriminate between directions and is excluded from the pre-registered test (reported for completeness: all three orderings agree with transfer on 2 of 3 benchmarks). A coverage-varying pretrained grid is the natural follow-up experiment.'

Full BFV recovery: KITTI-2015: dolly Delta 2.18, # movers 4, transl. 0.92, rot. 0.39, vert. frac 0.001, 'camera-centric (forward dolly)'; FlyingThings: dolly 0.32, # movers 2, transl. 1.41, rot. 1.36, vert. frac 0.920, 'object-centric (flying objects)'. Text admits the 'known blind spot': BFV is invariant to whether an aggregate field comes from camera motion or correspondingly moving objects.

Sampling stability: features recomputed at budgets 5x10^4 to 8x10^6 vectors across 'all 110 train->benchmark pairs'; mean-NN reaches rho >= 0.96 by 5x10^4 and 1.000 at the reference budget; epsilon-coverage at 4px similar; kNN-KL plateaus near rho=0.5 (T->B) and rho=0.2 (B->T) and never stabilizes. Also: 'Within the near-tied intervention family, the d_TB ranking remains estimator-noise-limited even after 5-seed averaging; out-of-sample correlations there are attenuated (conservative).'

Middlebury exclusion: pretrained variants returned '52.6 +/- 4.7 PCK regardless of training source (within-context spread 4.7 vs 10--17 on other benchmarks), while from-scratch variants spread normally (15.3)'; all reported numbers exclude Middlebury '(9 benchmarks, 1,458 models)'. Sensitivity: 'flip statistic +0.82 instead of +0.90; rule rho 0.49/0.50/0.52 instead of 0.50/0.51/0.51'; 'the largest single effect of the exclusion is on the pretrained-regime oracle fraction (0.554 -> 0.612 rule rho)'.

Figure captions: F5supp_decomposition: per-benchmark median slope '0.43--0.51 ~ rho, the reproducibility ceiling' (ranking) vs per-trainset median slope '0.93--0.96' (level anchor); F5grid_color_views: no single benchmark forms its own stripe post-exclusion, the pre-exclusion Middlebury defect was visible as such a stripe; F6_closed_loop: 'the null control realizes no gain, as predicted', Middlebury cell void.

claims.claim: Cross-reference baseline for the contradiction check: the main paper's account of the same pretrained grid arm reads 'its transfer compresses into a band a few seed-widths wide (3--8 PCK vs. 15--22 from scratch), so no ranking computed on it is stable; its unstable point estimates nominally favor the unmatched direction (d_TB +0.64, d_BT +0.31, sym +0.43)'.

red_flags.issue: The supplement's and the main paper's accounts of the pretrained intervention-grid arm contradict each other. Supp: the three sources' d_TB and d_BT orderings COINCIDE, so the arm 'cannot discriminate between directions' and 'all three orderings agree with transfer on 2 of 3 benchmarks'. Main: 'no ranking computed on it is stable; its unstable point estimates nominally favor the unmatched direction (d_TB +0.64, d_BT +0.31, sym +0.43)'. If the orderings truly coincided, Spearman vs transfer would be identical for both directions on every benchmark, so +0.64 vs +0.31 is impossible; the two documents also give different exclusion rationales (structural collinearity vs noise) and different summaries of the same excluded result.
